text:
sqlpipe moves Postgres tables into S3 as Parquet. Point it at a connection string and a bucket, name the tables you want, and it handles the rest: reading rows, writing columnar files, and uploading them. Full snapshots or incremental syncs based on a watermark column, so repeat runs only move what changed.

Output lands in a partitioned layout that Athena, DuckDB, Spark, and anything else speaking Parquet can query directly. No daemon, no scheduler, no coordination service — a single binary you run from cron, a CI job, or your own orchestrator. Configuration lives in one YAML file or command-line flags, whichever fits your setup. State is tracked in the bucket itself, so nothing extra to host and an interrupted run resumes rather than restarting.
